text.p: President Bill Clinton signed a budget bill into law before a midnight deadline on Monday, guaranteeing that the government would not shut down when the new fiscal year started on Tuesday.
Clinton signed the measure -- including money for his top spending priorities as well as funding for many government agencies -- hours after passage of the bill by the Senate, 84-15.

The law funded the military, national parks, education, jobs programmes, environmental protection and law enforcement, the White House, foreign aid, health research, and many other activities, combining six spending bills.

It also incorporated a once-contentious immigration bill and a badly needed measure to strengthen the thrift insurance fund. It included a measure ensuring that people who commit domestic crimes cannot purchase guns and it sold broadcast airwaves and expanded anti-terrorism measures.

The law provided $244 billion for the military and about $356 billion for other domestic programmes. The administration had wanted the military budget cut by $3.5 billion and asked for $10 billion in extra domestic spending.
Clinton won an extra $6.5 billion, including $4 billion for Head Start and other education programmes and raising college student Pell grants to the largest amount in history.
